title.en: New Chinese surveillance leaves foreigners nowhere to hide
title.zh: 中国新监控系统让外国人无处藏身

summary.en: A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."
summary.zh: 一位中国网络安全专家向德国之声披露了中国高科技警务的详细信息。该系统利用滑雪场的面部识别和火车座位等技术，可以追踪任何人并建立“综合档案”，让外国人无处藏身。

body.en:
A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."

When a cybersecurity researcher known by the pseudonym NetAskari recently clicked on a tab labeled "Inquiry for journalist files" on an unsecured Chinese web dashboard, he expected to see a jumble of auto-generated mock data.

Instead, familiar faces popped up on the screen. It was a comprehensive database of almost every foreign journalist based in the Chinese capital Beijing around 2021, including official passport photos taken at the entry/exit bureau, private cell phone numbers, visa details, and dates of birth. He also found his own exact personal information lying dormant on this Chinese police watchlist.

"It was more interesting than shocking," NetAskari told DW. "When you work as a journalist in China , you basically assume you are always on their radar. But what surprised me was simply how easy it was to access this highly sensitive system."

What NetAskari had stumbled upon is part modern China's emerging system of "holographic profiles."

He had unwittingly accessed a demonstration version of a remote tracking system designed for the Public Security Bureau in Zhangjiakou, the Hebei province city that hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics.

Though it was only a test panel, it was populated with real datasets, clearly outlining the trajectory of China's state surveillance machine, which is rapidly evolving from a network of simple street cameras into a data-fused, 24/7, predictive social control behemoth.

For years, China has operated the world's most extensive CCTV network. A massive initiative known as the "Xueliang" (Bright Eyes) project aims to merge these isolated islands of surveillance spread across the country.

But the data on the Zhangjiakou police dashboard shows the granular detail with which authorities can track an individual.

This system no longer relies solely on police cameras on street corners. It accurately records the specific train carriage and seat number a target occupies when arriving from Beijing or Shanghai.

It even synchronizes photos taken by facial-recognition ticket gates at local ski resorts directly into its tracking mechanism. The movements of the researcher's acquaintances who recently skied in Zhangjiakou were precisely flagged and mapped out with detailed trajectories in the system.

"The idea is simply to process as much data as possible from as many sensors as possible in real time," the researcher noted.

The system logs daily behaviors like gasoline consumption, regular shopping locations, and whether an individual frequently visits "petition areas."

body.zh: 一位中国网络安全专家向德国之声透露了中国新型高科技警务的细节。从滑雪场面部识别到火车座位，该系统可以跟踪任何人并编制“整体档案”。 当一位化名 NetAskari 的网络安全研究人员最近点击一个不安全的中文网络仪表板上标有“查询记者档案”的选项卡时，他预计会看到一堆自动生成的模拟数据。 取而代之的是，熟悉的面孔出现在屏幕上。这是 2021 年左右驻扎在中国首都北京的几乎所有外国记者的综合数据库，包括在出入境管理局拍摄的官方护照照片、私人手机号码、签证详细信息和出生日期。他还发现自己的确切个人信息隐藏在中国警方的监视名单上。 “这比令人震惊更有趣，”内特阿斯卡里告诉德国之声。 “当你在中国担任记者时，你基本上会认为你总是在他们的监视范围内。但令我惊讶的是访问这个高度敏感的系统是多么容易。” NetAskari 偶然发现的是现代中国新兴的“全息轮廓”系统的一部分。 他无意中访问了为主办 2022 年冬季奥运会的河北省张家口市公安局设计的远程跟踪系统演示版本。 虽然它只是一个测试面板，但它填充了真实的数据集，清楚地概述了中国国家监控机器的轨迹，该机器正在从简单的街道摄像头网络迅速演变为数据融合的、24/7、预测性的社会控制庞然大物。 多年来，中国运营着世界上最广泛的闭路电视网络。一项名为“雪亮”（明亮的眼睛）项目的大规模倡议旨在合并这些分布在全国各地的监视孤岛。 但张家口警方仪表板上的数据显示了当局可以追踪个人的详细信息。 该系统不再仅仅依赖街角的警察摄像头。它准确记录目标从北京或上海到达时所占用的具体火车车厢和座位号。 它甚至将当地滑雪场的面部识别检票口拍摄的照片直接同步到其跟踪机制中。研究人员最近在张家口滑雪的熟人的动作被精确标记，并在系统中绘制出详细的轨迹。 研究人员指出：“这个想法只是实时处理来自尽可能多的传感器的尽可能多的数据。” 该系统记录日常行为，例如汽油消耗、常规购物地点以及个人是否经常访问“请愿区”。 这项大规模的数据融合工作试图……

reflection.en: The news of pervasive surveillance systems highlights the immense power states can wield over individuals. When such power is unchecked, it can feel like living under constant scrutiny, eroding personal freedom and privacy. This reminds us of the biblical warning about rulers who oppress their people, creating an environment of fear rather than security.
reflection.zh: 普遍存在的监控系统新闻突显了国家对个人可能施加的巨大权力。当这种权力不受制约时，人们可能会感到生活在持续的审视之下，个人自由和隐私受到侵蚀。这提醒我们圣经中关于压迫人民、制造恐惧而非安全的统治者的警告。

title.en: 'My dear friend': Putin and Xi praise partnership during talks in Beijing
title.zh: “我的挚友”：普京和习近平在北京会谈中赞扬伙伴关系

summary.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping praised their partnership during talks in Beijing. China continues to be a significant and loyal economic partner to Russia, despite international economic and financial sanctions imposed on Russia by other countries.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯总统普京和中国国家主席习近平在北京会谈期间赞扬了两国伙伴关系。尽管其他国家对俄罗斯实施了经济和金融制裁，中国仍然是俄罗斯重要而忠诚的经济伙伴。

body.en:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has lauded his close ties with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, saying the nations are partners in trade and international affairs during bilateral talks in Beijing.

Xi welcomed Putin with a ceremony at the Great Hall of the People only days after meeting United States President Donald Trump.

The quick succession of Trump's and Putin's visits highlighted China's growing role as an international superpower, experts say.

Putin greeted Xi warmly as they met for the bilateral talks, describing the Chinese president as a "dear friend".

"We are truly delighted to see you. We keep in constant touch, both personally and through our aides in the government," he said.

Xi also stressed the "political mutual trust and strategic co-operation" between the countries, according to Chinese state media.

The two leaders have praised each other profusely in the past — Xi once describing Putin as his "best and most intimate friend".

Xi and Putin were set to focus on energy and security as well as their overall ties.

Chinese state media reported both parties agreed to extend a friendship treaty first signed in 2001.

China became Russia's top trading partner after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

China has said it is neutral in the conflict, maintaining trade ties with Russia despite economic and financial sanctions against Russia by the US and Europe.

China is the top customer for Russian oil and gas supplies, and Russia expects the war in Iran to increase the demand.

"The driving force behind economic co-operation is Russian-Chinese collaboration in the energy sector," Putin said.

"Amid the crisis in the Middle East, Russia continues to maintain its role as a reliable supplier of resources, while China remains a responsible consumer of these resources."

Xi stressed the need for the "complete cessation of hostilities" in the Middle East, according to Chinese state media.

"An early end to the conflict will help reduce disruptions to energy supply stability, the smooth flow of industrial and supply chains, and international trade order," Xi said.

A Russian presidential aide said earlier that Russia's oil exports to China grew by 35 per cent in the first quarter of 2026. Russia was also one of the biggest exporters of natural gas to China.

Putin said China and Russia's co-operation in foreign policy is "one of the key stabilising factors on the international stage".

In February 2022, just weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine, China and Russia announced a "no limits" partnership during a trip by Putin to Beijing.

Despite taking a neutral stance in the conflict, China supports Russia through frequent state visits, growing trade and joint military drills.

This verse reminds us that the choices nations make, especially in their alliances and economic dealings, contribute to their moral standing and reputation among the peoples of the world. May leaders seek wisdom to guide their countries in ways that bring honor...

summary.en: Young chess players are quickly achieving success and winning competitions, often against older rivals, but are subsequently choosing to leave the sport. The article suggests there's an underlying reason for this pattern of early achievement followed by disengagement.

Without a word, Clarissa Liu softly shakes her opponent's hand at a chess club in Brisbane.

The room is silent — except for the offbeat clicking of chess clocks and the faint sounds of scribbling on paper.

Her fluffy pink-and-yellow cardigan stands out in the crowd, where each player is fixated on the board in front of them.

Like many times before, the nine-year-old is about to win a game of chess against a man more than twice her age.

"So, I like more girl chess players, and when I see people around me that are girls, I feel happy and I want to win," Liu tells SBS News.

While chess has found a new audience through pop culture and online platforms, many female players say the competitive world still feels overwhelmingly male, prompting questions around why so few girls continue playing into adulthood.

Popular streaming content, such as drama series The Queen's Gambit and a recent documentary about Hungarian chess champion Judit Polgár, has again put a spotlight on the experiences of women in the game.

Chess.com, the world's largest online chess platform, says it has surpassed 250 million members worldwide, with nearly 15 million new accounts created in the first three months of 2026 alone.

But despite chess soaring in popularity, the number of women playing at an elite level remains low.

Girls and women make up just 16.5 per cent of the world's 1.4 million active chess players, according to the International Chess Federation's (FIDE) 2026 Gender Equality in Chess Index (GECI) report.

Queensland-based Eleanor Wu is the 2025 Australian under-8 girls' chess champion.

She is also one of the few young female players at her club and says she gets frustrated when she hears chess described as a game for boys.

"Some of my friends say girls shouldn't play chess because they aren't smart enough," Wu tells SBS News.

While there are more than 1,500 chess grandmasters worldwide — the highest title a player can achieve — less than 50 are women.

Grandmaster David Smerdon, an associate professor in the school of economics at the University of Queensland, started playing at the age of five after finding a board in his attic.

Smerdon has since represented Australia at the Chess Olympiad, an international team chess tournament organised by FIDE.

He believes women face additional barriers in competitive chess, contributing to many teenage girls dropping out of the game in Australia.

"As soon as school finishes and they have to go to their first open tournament, there might be 100 men in the room and three girls, and suddenly you don't have that same social connection," Smerdon tells SBS News.

While temporary victories bring acclaim, they may not offer the lasting purpose or satisfaction that sustains long-term engagement. This reminds us to consider what kind of "crown" we are truly striving for.
reflection.zh: 年轻棋手早早获胜却又放弃比赛的故事，突显了世俗成就的短暂性。虽然暂时的胜利能带来赞誉，但它们可能无法提供维持长期投入的持久目标或满足感。这提醒我们思考，我们真正追求的是哪一种“冠冕”。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: The numbers don't tell the whole story about Australia's biggest migrant group
title.zh: “回老家去”：澳大利亚移民辩论的丑陋一面

summary.en: As the topic of migration becomes a central issue in Australian politics, Indian Australians report experiencing personal social costs, including hostile sentiments like being told to "go back home."
summary.zh: 随着移民问题在澳大利亚政治中占据主导地位，印度裔澳大利亚人表示，他们正在经历个人层面的社会代价，包括被告知“回老家去”等敌意言论。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

For some Indian Australians, these words are no longer confined to fringe corners of the internet. As migration numbers dominate political and public debate, community leaders say they are increasingly part of daily life — cropping up in social media comment sections, on public transport, in workplaces and neighbourhood conversations.

The latest Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data places India at the centre of Australia's migration story. For the first time on record, people born in India are the largest overseas-born group in the country, narrowly surpassing those born in England in 2025.

Of the 8.83 million Australian residents born overseas, 971,020 were born in India as of 30 June 2025, reflecting steady growth in Indian migration over the past four years.

But behind the headlines and political arguments over migration is a more confronting reality emerging within parts of the Indian Australian community: a growing awareness that migrants are being blamed for pressures linked to housing, infrastructure and the rising cost of living.

Researchers and community advocates say racist abuse and anti-Indian rhetoric have intensified in recent years, amplified online amid increasingly politicised migration debates and public protests .

The concerns echo warnings from Australia's human rights sector. Last month, Australian Human Rights Commission president Hugh de Kretser warned that rising racism and political polarisation risk undermining social cohesion, particularly when migrant communities are treated as threats or blamed for broader issues.

Launching the commission's inaugural annual human rights assessment, he pointed to recent anti-migration rallies, saying migrants from India, Muslim communities and people of Lebanese and Palestinian backgrounds had all been targeted in public discourse.

"These attacks on migrants must stop," de Kretser said in his National Press Club address.

Migration experts say much of the debate often lacks key context, including ongoing domestic labour shortages, post-COVID-19 migration flows and Australia's economic reliance on skilled migrants and international students.

As India takes on a leading role in Australia's migration story, the debate is no longer only about population numbers. It has become a test of how Australia balances social cohesion, economic need and multicultural identity amid rising anxiety and political tensions.

ABS figures show Indian-born residents have been among the fastest-growing overseas-born groups in Australia in recent years, mainly driven by international education and skilled migration pathways.

Abul Rizvi, former deputy secretary of the immigration department, says...
body.zh: 分享您的反馈并帮助我们改进此功能。请在此处详细了解我们如何在 SBS 使用人工智能。 对于一些印度裔澳大利亚人来说，这些词不再局限于互联网的边缘角落。随着移民数量主导政治和公共辩论，社区领导人表示，移民越来越成为日常生活的一部分——出现在社交媒体评论部分、公共交通、工作场所和邻里对话中。 澳大利亚统计局（ABS）的最新数据将印度置于澳大利亚移民故事的中心。有记录以来，印度出生的人口首次成为该国最大的海外出生群体，到 2025 年将微弱地超过英国出生的人口。 截至2025年6月30日，在海外出生的883万澳大利亚居民中，有971,020人在印度出生，反映出过去四年印度移民的稳定增长。 但在有关移民的头条新闻和政治争论的背后，是印裔澳大利亚社区部分地区出现的一个更加严峻的现实：人们越来越认识到，住房、基础设施和生活成本上涨等压力都归咎于移民。 研究人员和社区倡导者表示，近年来，种族主义辱骂和反印度言论愈演愈烈，随着移民辩论和公众抗议日益政治化，这些言论在网上进一步放大。 这些担忧呼应了澳大利亚人权部门的警告。上个月，澳大利亚人权委员会主席休·德克雷泽警告说，日益严重的种族主义和政治两极分化可能会破坏社会凝聚力，特别是当移民社区被视为威胁或因更广泛的问题而受到指责时。 在启动委员会首次年度人权评估时，他提到了最近的反移民集会，称来自印度、穆斯林社区以及黎巴嫩和巴勒斯坦背景的移民都成为公共言论的目标。 “这些针对移民的袭击必须停止，”德克雷泽在全国新闻俱乐部讲话中说。 移民专家表示，大部分辩论往往缺乏关键背景，包括持续的国内劳动力短缺、COVID-19 后的移民流动以及澳大利亚对技术移民和国际学生的经济依赖。 随着印度在澳大利亚移民故事中发挥主导作用，争论不再仅仅是关于人口数量。它已成为澳大利亚如何在焦虑和政治紧张局势加剧的情况下平衡社会凝聚力、经济需求和多元文化身份的考验。 ABS数据显示，近年来，印度出生的居民一直是澳大利亚增长最快的海外出生群体之一，这主要是由国际教育和技术移民途径推动的。 移民部前副部长阿布尔·里兹维 (Abul Rizvi) 表示……

reflection.en: The rising hostility towards migrants, as reported in Australia, highlights a timeless challenge: how societies treat those who come from other lands. Scripture reminds us to welcome the foreigner among us, treating them as native-born and loving them as ourselves. This call to empathy and hospitality transcends political rhetoric, urging us to see the...
reflection.zh: 正如报道中所述，澳大利亚对移民日益增长的敌意，凸显了一个永恒的挑战：社会如何对待来自异乡的人。圣经提醒我们，要欢迎寄居在我们中间的外国人，待他们如同本地人一样，爱他们如同自己。这种对同理心和好客的呼唤超越了政治言论，敦促我们看到每个人身上共同的人性。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: $10bn wipeout: Why investors are suddenly worried about an Australian giant
title.zh: 100亿澳元蒸发：投资者为何突然担忧这家澳大利亚巨头？

summary.en: CSL, one of Australia's most trusted companies, experienced a dramatic collapse, leading to a $10 billion wipeout and shattering investor confidence.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚最受信任的公司之一CSL遭遇了戏剧性的崩溃，导致100亿澳元的市值蒸发，并严重打击了投资者的信心。

body.en:
For years, CSL was seen as one of Australia's safest blue-chip investments — a healthcare giant trusted by super funds, retail investors and the broader market.

But in recent weeks, the biotech company's share price has suffered one of the sharpest falls in its history, wiping nearly $10 billion from its market value.

What kicked off that major price plunge was the company's announcement on 11 May, which revealed massive business write-downs and a downgrade of future profit expectations.

While the shock announcement rattled investors, the company's share price had been on a downward spiral long before that.

The events now raise a broader question: is this a temporary stumble for one of Australia's corporate champions, or a sign it has deeper problems?

Speaking to SBS On the Money on 11 May, Munjarra Capital chief executive Alex Pikoulas put it simply: "This is no longer the same company with the same outlook that everyone fell in love with years ago".

Investment analyst Richard Hemming from Under the Radar Report said many of the company's current problems could be traced back to acquisitions it had made, particularly the multi-billion-dollar purchase of kidney treatment business Vifor in 2022.

The Melbourne-based biotechnology company stunned markets after it said on 11 May that it would book around US$5 billion (A$6.9 billion) in impairment charges against its Vifor business, which reduced its profit massively for the 2026 financial year.

In simple terms, an impairment means writing off parts of a business that are worth significantly less than previously thought.

CSL also warned that the expected growth it had projected would take longer to materialise than it had anticipated.

It had been hit by weaker vaccination demand in the United States after the pandemic-era surge faded, and has faced rising competition in iron deficiency treatments and ongoing pricing pressure in China's albumin market.

At the same time, higher plasma collection costs have squeezed margins, and a period of executive turnover and restructuring has added to investor uncertainty about the company's direction.

Hemming said those pressures had compounded broader concerns about whether CSL could ultimately deliver the growth investors had expected.

Munjarra's Pikoulas said investors were also confronting the reality that CSL was operating in a far more competitive environment than the one that helped build its reputation over previous decades.

"A lot has changed, in particular the competitive environment they're facing, which has been a big contributor to these downgrades," he said.

He also said there was "a lot of uncertainty" at the top of the company, which is currently led by an interim chief executive while its chief commercial officer prepares to...
body.zh: 多年来，CSL 被视为澳大利亚最安全的蓝筹投资之一——一家受到超级基金、散户投资者和更广泛市场信赖的医疗保健巨头。 但最近几周，这家生物技术公司的股价遭遇了历史上最严重的跌幅之一，市值蒸发了近 100 亿美元。 引发价格大幅下跌的是该公司 5 月 11 日的公告，该公告披露了大规模的业务减记和未来利润预期的下调。 尽管这一令人震惊的公告令投资者感到不安，但该公司的股价在此之前很久就一直处于螺旋式下降状态。 这些事件现在引发了一个更广泛的问题：这对于澳大利亚企业冠军之一来说是暂时的绊脚石，还是表明它存在更深层次的问题？ 5 月 11 日，Munjarra Capital 首席执行官 Alex Pikoulas 在接受 SBS On the Money 采访时简单地说：“这不再是几年前每个人都爱上的同一家具有相同前景的公司”。 Under the Radar Report 的投资分析师理查德·海明 (Richard Hemming) 表示，该公司当前的许多问题可以追溯到其进行的收购，特别是 2022 年斥资数十亿美元收购肾脏治疗业务 Vifor。 这家总部位于墨尔本的生物技术公司于 5 月 11 日表示，将为其 Vifor 业务计入约 50 亿美元（69 亿澳元）的减值费用，此举震惊了市场，这导致其 2026 财年的利润大幅下降。 简单来说，减值意味着注销价值远低于先前预期的部分业务。 CSL还警告说，其预计的增长将需要比预期更长的时间才能实现。 在大流行时代的激增消退后，该公司受到美国疫苗接种需求疲软的打击，并面临缺铁治疗日益激烈的竞争以及中国白蛋白市场持续的定价压力。 与此同时，较高的血浆采集成本挤压了利润率，一段时期的高管更替和重组增加了投资者对公司发展方向的不确定性。 海明表示，这些压力加剧了人们对中超联赛能否最终实现投资者预期增长的更广泛担忧。 Munjarra 的 Pikoulas 表示，投资者还面临这样一个现实，即 CSL 的运营环境比过去几十年帮助其建立声誉的环境竞争激烈得多。 他说：“很多事情都发生了变化，特别是他们面临的竞争环境，这是导致评级下调的一个重要因素。” 他还表示，该公司高层存在“很多不确定性”，目前该公司由临时首席执行官领导，而其首席商务官则准备......

reflection.en: The dramatic collapse of a trusted company and the resulting financial loss remind us of the transient nature of earthly treasures. While we strive for stability, this event underscores the wisdom in not placing our ultimate security in wealth that can be destroyed or lost. It invites us to consider where our true and lasting treasures lie.
reflection.zh: 一家备受信任的公司突然崩溃，以及随之而来的巨大经济损失，提醒我们世上财宝的短暂性。尽管我们努力追求稳定，但这一事件强调了不要将最终的安全感寄托在可能被毁坏或失去的财富上的智慧。它邀请我们思考我们真正持久的财宝在哪里。

title.en: Samuel's visa status made him easier to exploit. A new project hopes to help migrants like him
title.zh: 塞缪尔的签证身份让他更容易被剥削。一个新项目希望能帮助像他一样的移民

summary.en: A new initiative in New South Wales aims to assist temporary visa holders who face exploitation and other workplace issues, recognizing their heightened vulnerability.
summary.zh: 新南威尔士州的一项新计划旨在帮助面临剥削和其他工作场所问题的临时签证持有者，认识到他们的高度脆弱性。

body.en:
After arriving in Sydney from Colombia, Samuel Zuluaga felt lucky to find an employer willing to sponsor his temporary work visa.

While the 23-year-old hoped the barber shop job would help him build a stable future, he was underpaid, missed out on superannuation payments and feared speaking up because his visa depended on him remaining with his employer.

"After about a year, I noticed my employer had stopped paying my superannuation," Zuluaga told SBS News.

"At that time, I didn't fully understand what that meant. I told myself it might be a mistake."

Zuluaga said he was reluctant to raise concerns because he feared jeopardising his work rights in Australia.

"One day, I complained when I was asked to clean the toilet, knowing that it wasn't my responsibility," he said.

"My employer just said, 'You are fired, pack your stuff and go home'. Just like that, I had lost my job and my visa sponsor."

Zuluaga also alleges he was denied payment for unused annual leave because he was too afraid to take time off work.

Eventually, with support from unions and advocacy services, he recovered the money he was owed.

"It wasn't just about the money. It changed my situation and showed me that I wasn't alone."

Zuluaga's experience reflects broader concerns raised in a recent report by the Migrant Justice Institute, which found nearly two-thirds of temporary visa holders surveyed had experienced underpayment.

The report also estimated that international students alone are losing more than $60 million in wages every week.

More than a third of respondents reported working under Australian Business Number (ABN) or contractor arrangements.

Previous reports have identified limited English, poor awareness of workplace rights and difficulty accessing support services as factors increasing the risk of exploitation.

Unions NSW president Mark Morey said that, despite this mistreatment, migrant workers played a critical role in Australia's economy.

title.en: Melbourne teenager becomes youngest Australian to summit Mount Everest
title.zh: 墨尔本少年成为最年轻的澳大利亚珠穆朗玛峰登顶者

summary.en: The 18-year-old's singular achievement comes as the number of climbers ascending to the world's tallest peak hits a record high.
summary.zh: 这位18岁少年独特的成就，正值登顶世界最高峰的登山者人数创下历史新高之际。

body.en:
An 18-year-old from Melbourne has become the youngest Australian to summit Mount Everest, reaching the peak of the world's tallest mountain on her second attempt.

Bianca Adler completed the ascent of the 8,849-metre summit alongside two Nepali guides, surpassing the previous Australian record holders Alyssa Azar and Gabby Kanizay.

Her ascent comes as the daily number of climbers summiting Everest from the Nepal side hits a record high of 274. Concerns over overcrowding, congestion in the 'death zone' at the top of the world's tallest mountain and threats to climber safety have been going on for years.

Speaking to SBS Nepali after returning to Kathmandu, Adler described the physical exhaustion of the climb and the relief of finally turning back down the mountain.

"It's a mix of emotions because it feels amazing to reach the top and on the other hand, just to stop going up because it is quite tiring," she said.

"It's really exhausting being at those altitudes because there is a really little amount of oxygen."

Adler said the descent was among the toughest parts of the expedition, after completing a gruelling 23-hour push from Camp Four to the summit and back to Camp Two.

"We arrived at base camp in the morning, ate a little bit and then had to pack up all our gear that we had spread out over the past few months," she said.

Despite the physical strain, Adler said her previous mountaineering experience helped her body adapt to the extreme conditions.

"With experience on other mountains, my body has sort of learned how to adapt a little bit better to those higher altitudes and how to function better on less food and water."

Adler spent about 20 minutes at the summit, reaching the top around 2:20am local time.

"It's a really amazing moment knowing you have reached the top of the world," she said.

"But we also have to go down and we are only halfway at the top and most of the accidents happen on the way down, so you also have to stay focused."

She said overcrowding near the summit meant climbers had to briefly wait their turn at the peak.

"We were the second group at the summit that day so you need to let everyone have their moment at the top of the world," she said.

"We also have to be super mindful not to take our big gloves off for too long because that is how you get frostbite."

Adler praised fellow Australian climbers Alyssa Azar and Gabby Kanizay, and said they had inspired her own mountaineering ambitions.

"Ever since a few years ago when I was training for other mountains, I had just looked up to those women," she said.

reflection.en: The ascent of Mount Everest demands immense discipline, training, and perseverance, much like an athlete striving for a perishable crown. This remarkable feat reminds us of the human spirit's capacity to push limits. Yet, it also invites us to consider what "crown" we are ultimately striving for, and whether it is one that will last eternally.
reflection.zh: 攀登珠穆朗玛峰需要巨大的纪律、训练和毅力，就像运动员为那会朽坏的冠冕而努力一样。这项非凡的壮举提醒我们人类精神突破极限的能力。然而，它也邀请我们思考我们最终追求的是怎样的“冠冕”，以及它是否是永恒不朽的。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。
